title: The City Hidden Behind One Basement Wall
hook_sentence: In 1963, a man renovating his house in Cappadocia knocked through a wall and found a tunnel.
narration_script: In 1963, a man renovating his house in Cappadocia knocked through a wall and found a tunnel. It led into Derinkuyu, an underground city carved roughly eighty-five metres down into soft volcanic rock. Its levels held stables, wells, chapels and food stores, while dozens of ventilation shafts carried fresh air to the deepest rooms. Rolling stone doors, some weighing up to half a ton, sealed each level from the inside. Its earliest tunnels may be nearly three thousand years old, and Byzantine-era Christians later expanded it to hide from raids. For centuries, an entire city lay hidden beneath ordinary homes, waiting behind a single wall.
closing_sentence: For centuries, an entire city lay hidden beneath ordinary homes, waiting behind a single wall.
caption:
One renovation. One wall. One forgotten city.

In 1963, a resident of Derinkuyu in central Turkey broke through a wall in his home and found the entrance to a vast underground settlement. Carved into soft volcanic tuff, it held stables, wells, chapels and storerooms, sealed by rolling stone doors. Its earliest phases may date back to the first millennium BC, and it was greatly expanded in the Byzantine era as a refuge from raids.

Could you spend weeks underground to stay safe?

📍 Derinkuyu, Nevşehir, Turkey
